properties.content:

Violation ID: 885988
Permit API: 117-21935
Unconventional: Yes
County: Tioga
Municipality: Liberty Twp
Inspection Type: Administrative/File Review
Inspection Date: 2020-06-03
Comments: Inspection conducted in response to a notification from the operator of a release of produced water which occurred during fracing operations. The operator initially estimated the release to be approximately 20 gallons. The release was reported to have occurred due to a failed valve on a water truck which had been in the process of unloading produced water into a holding tank. In a follow-up email sent on 6/1/20 by Mike Deming of SWN, the estimated release volume was decreased to less than 20 gallons. The email also stated that the fluid was immediately removed from the pad surface by a vacuum truck and visually impacted material was excavated and placed in a lined roll-off box to await proper disposal. The size of the excavation area was 20 ft by 25 ft and an average depth of 2 inches. The estimated volume of material excavated was reported as less than 1 cubic yard. Violations noted and considered immediately corrected.

properties.content:
Report Details
Operator: Diversified Oil & Gas Llc
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 2019-04-02
Violation Code: SWMA 610(1) - UNLAWFUL CONDUCT - Person dumped or deposited, or permitted the dumping or depositing, of solid waste onto the surface of the ground or underground or into the waters of the Commonwealth, without a permit for the dumping of such solid wastes from DEP.
Violation ID: 845632
Permit API: 065-26370
Unconventional: No
County: Jefferson
Municipality: Heath Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 2019-04-02
Comments: This well was drilled in a forested area off of Spring Creek Road in July 2008. A spill was reported to the Department at 16:28 on April 1, 2019. The spill occurred when the brine tank overflowed. Oil was allowed to escape and contact the ground surface, but no evidence of a brine discharge could be seen. The reported release amount was of approximately 30 gallons, and conditions at the site at the time of inspection indicate that this estimate is reasonable. Because the estimated spill volume was less than 1 bbl, a visual clean-up at this site is appropriate. A culvert under the access road has overtopped, allowing sediment to be carried into the stream in this HQ watershed. As per a phone call with Joshua Martz from Diversified at 11:50 on April 2, equipment is expected to arrive on site in the morning of April 3. The visual cleanup of the site is expected to be completed at that time. You are hereby requested to follow Department Policy 800-5000-001, Addressing Spills and Releases at Oil & Gas Well Sites or Access Road. This Policy sets forth the procedures that should be followed to resolve the violations associated with the spill/discharge/release noted in this Notice of Violation by using either the Act 2 or the Alternative Remediation Process. A copy of the Policy is attached for your review.

properties.content:

Violation Code: SWMA 301 - MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person operated a residual waste processing or disposal facility without obtaining a permit for such facility from DEP. Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
Violation ID: 8206163
Permit API: 081-21989
Unconventional: Yes
County: Lycoming
Municipality: Plunketts Creek Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 10/28/2024
Comments: Arrived onsite in response to a reported release of a petroleum based fluid. The release was found by Zac Subra around 12:30 pm on Monday, 10/28/24. Over the preceding weekend, containment was being pulled and placed into dumpsters for disposal.The impacted area was estimated to be about 50' by 100' although the surface staining was not continuous throughout the entire area. The impacts were just to the southwest of the wells. The actual size of the release will be better known as the impacted area is excavated.Around the time the release was discovered, it was noted that one of the dumpsters holding containment was leaking some sort of fluid. The dumpster was placed on secondary containment to further evaluate its contents and ensure that it is suitable to travel on the road. The leaking dumpster created a second impacted area that was approximately 25' by 15'. This second location was near the edge of the pad roughly south of the original impacted area.At the time of inspection, there was no evidence of impacts beyond the pad surface. Tobias was expected to begin excavating the impacted area before the end of the day. Penn E and R was also scheduled to begin sampling for remediation under Act 2.The result of this inspection is Violations Noted for CSL 402(b), SWMA 301, and 78a56(a).

Report Details
Inspection Client: EQT ARO LLC

Violation Date: 12/22/2023
Violation Code: 78a56(a) - TEMPORARY STORAGE - Operator failed to contain regulated substances and wastes used at or generated at a well site in a tank, series of tanks or other storage structures approved by the Department.
Violation ID: 8169389
Permit API: 081-21908
Unconventional: Yes
County: Lycoming
Municipality: Cascade Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 12/22/2023
Comments: On December 22, 2023, DEP representative Brad Kline conducted an incident inspection at the EQT ARO LLC Salt Run Hunting Club Pad A Extension. EQT reported a spill of approximately 300 gallons of glycol outside of containment and onto the well pad surface on the morning of December 22, 2023. Upon arrival, DEP spoke with EQT Rick Hall and he said that a valve fitting failed on one of the dehydration units. This caused glycol to mist onto the well pad surface. The area of impact was about 60 feet by 60 feet, in an "L" shape due to the dehydration equipment being in place. The depth of the impact to the well pad surface was unknown at the time of the inspection. Excavation of the area had not begun while DEP was onsite. EQT was waiting on equipment to be delivered to the well pad to begin the excavation around the dehydration unit and gas lines. A plan was still being developed by EQT to clean off the equipment that the glycol came in contact with. EQT plans to have Penn E and R begin the Act 2 remediation process. DEP spoke with Mr. Hall on December 26, 2023. The equipment that the glycol came in contact with was washed down. Mr. Hall said that the excavation of the impacted area was completed late on December 22, 2023. Confirmatory samples were collected and Mr. Hall provided DEP with pictures of the excavated area. The spill of glycol outside of containment onto the well pad surface is a violation of the Clean Streams Law 402(b), Solid Waste Management Act Section 301, and Chapter 78a.56(a).

A 5x Altair gas meter was used to screen around the production equipment. No combustible or methane gases were detected. A future inspection will be conducted to ensure that the initial remediation efforts were sufficient.

Violation Code: SWMA 301 - MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person operated a residual waste processing or disposal facility without obtaining a permit for such facility from DEP. Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
Violation ID: 835627
Permit API: 059-27587
Unconventional: Yes
County: Greene
Municipality: Richhill Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 2018-12-03
Comments: On December 3, 2018, the Department performed an inspection of the CNX RHL22 well pad site, with Kevin Maskol (DEP). Present at time of inspection was Kyle Borden, Spencer Johnson, and Jason Harding (CNX). The site is located in Richhill Twp., Greene County. The inspection was a incident inspection related to a reported reuse water release to the well pad. The operator initially reported a 30 barrel reuse water release to the well pad @ 01:15 a.m. on 12/1/18. The operator did contact the Department at 11:00 a.m. on 12/1/18 to report that the release was greater and was approximately 210 barrels of reuse water. The operator has reported that during the transfer of reuse water from the constructed MASS on the tank pad, along the access road, to the working tanks a communication error occurred and the working tanks were over filled causing a release of approximately 210 barrels of reuse water to the well pad. The reuse water overwhelmed the well pad secondary containment discharging to the well pad and storm water collection channels for the site. The reuse water then entered the PCSM structure discharging off site. The collection channel to the PCSM was also overwhelmed and the water was discharged onto the RHL28 gathering pipeline ROW adjacent to the well pad site. The operator was excavating impacted material off site on the pipeline ROW at time of inspection. The operator was using field conductivity readings to direct the excavation activities. The operator had attempted to plug the PCSM discharge structure, with an inflatable rubber plug, but was unable to do so. The Department observed elevated conductivity readings in the standing water and soils on the southwest corner of the well pad, as well as the storm water controls for this area. Elevated conductivity readings were also observed off the well pad site on the pipeline ROW and down gradient from both sites. At the time of the inspection the A, B, C, and D wells were being zipper fracked. The MASS was observed. It is located on a tank pad several hundred feet north of the well pad at an elevation of 1284. This is approximately 30' higher than the elevation of the well pad at 1253.5. It is not clear at this time if gravity had any effect on the incident. It was a 21K Bbl primary containment structure inside of a 24 K Bbl secondary containment structure. The tank manufacturer was Rain For Rent. This appears to match the approved OG-71B for the site. DEP recommends that CNX implement new engineering controls and operational changes to allow for emergency shut offs in the event of a release or other emergency during water transfer from an approved MASS to the frac.”

Comments: On 4/24/2026, the Department conducted a surface inspection at the Clara Jacques 1 well site in Wharton Township, Fayette County. This inspection was conducted in response to a Notice of Intent (NOI) to plug the well, which was submitted by the operator on 4/20/2026. A Consent Order and Agreement (COA) was entered into between the Department and Diversified on 3/07/2019. According to the COA, Diversified is to restore the Well Site after in accordance with Section 3216 of the 2012 Oil and Gas Act, 58 Pa. C.S.A. 3216; after completion of plugging operations.The following was observed during the inspection:A Rock Construction Entrance (RCE) is installed at the site entrance along Five Forks Road (photos 1 and 2). The Erosion and Sedimentation (E and S) control plan available is on site (photos 13-16). An additional RCE is installed where the access road meets the well site, in accordance with the E and S plan drawing (photo 11). Compost Filter Sock (CFS) is installed on site in the locations shown on E and S plan drawing (photos 9, 12, 17, 19, and 20). Some tire rutting was observed in the access road. The tire rutting appears to be severe in the location shown in Photo 7. Due to the soft and damp soil conditions that appear to exist on site, the Department recommends that the operator consider additional E and S control measures as necessary, to prevent accelerated erosion and sedimentation from occurring on site. Representatives from Next Level Energy were observed staging well plugging equipment during this inspection. No evidence of a spill, such as staining, was observed on site during this inspection. The API number and operator's information are posted on the disconnected meter box at the time of inspection (photo 18). Based on observations from this inspection, violations are being issued against the severe tire rutting in the access road.The Department observed an access road cross-culvert (photo 23). No loose sediment was observed in the cross-culvert during this inspection. However, the Department recommends that the operator take necessary measures to ensure that the cross-culvert is protected from sedimentation. Comments: On 4/24/2026, the Department conducted a surface inspection at the Clara Jacques 1 well site in Wharton Township, Fayette County. This inspection was conducted in response to a Notice of Intent (NOI) to plug the well, which was submitted by the operator on 4/20/2026. A Consent Order and Agreement (COA) was entered into between the Department and Diversified on 3/07/2019. According to the COA, Diversified is to restore the Well Site after in accordance with Section 3216 of the 2012 Oil and Gas Act, 58 Pa. C.S.A. 3216; after completion of plugging operations.The following was observed during the inspection:A Rock Construction Entrance (RCE) is installed at the site entrance along Five Forks Road (photos 1 and 2). The Erosion and Sedimentation (E and S) control plan available is on site (photos 13-16). An additional RCE is installed where the access road meets the well site, in accordance with the E and S plan drawing (photo 11). Compost Filter Sock (CFS) is installed on site in the locations shown on E and S plan drawing (photos 9, 12, 17, 19, and 20). Some tire rutting was observed in the access road. The tire rutting appears to be severe in the location shown in Photo 7. Due to the soft and damp soil conditions that appear to exist on site, the Department recommends that the operator consider additional E and S control measures as necessary, to prevent accelerated erosion and sedimentation from occurring on site. Representatives from Next Level Energy were observed staging well plugging equipment during this inspection. No evidence of a spill, such as staining, was observed on site during this inspection. The API number and operator's information are posted on the disconnected meter box at the time of inspection (photo 18). Based on observations from this inspection, violations are being issued against the severe tire rutting in the access road.The Department observed an access road cross-culvert (photo 23). No loose sediment was observed in the cross-culvert during this inspection. However, the Department recommends that the operator take necessary measures to ensure that the cross-culvert is protected from sedimentation. Additional violations may be forthcoming pending re-assessment and re-evaluation of this location in a future inspection.

Comments: On 03/12/25 an incident inspection of the Decker 1 Well Site was conducted in response to the report of a spill received by the Department on 03/12/25. (CTS: 387446). Background:On 03/12/25 Greylock self-reported a brine release at the Decker 1 well. On 03/12/25 I spoke to Trevor Woods of Greylock to acquire additional details about the spill. During the inspection it was determined that an unknown amount but over 5 gallons of produced water had been released to the well area from a failure on the bottom of the tank. Investigation showed that the release was contained to the well area and no water ways were impacted. Remediation efforts were underway at the time of my inspection. Findings:-No distressed vegetation was observed in the spill area. -The spill is suspected to have originated from a crack on the bottom of the tank (Photo #7).-Elevated conductivity was observed in the substrate in the spill area (Photos #4-5). -Crews were present on-site working to remediate the spill. (Photos #2-3, 6). -No elevated conductivity was observed outside of the spill area.No discharge to surface water was observed.Remediation efforts were nearing completion as I was leaving the site. Violations of 78.57(a), SWMA 301, and 78.54 are being issued for the release of brine to the ground.

Comments: On December 3, 2025, the Department conducted a follow-up inspection to IR 4088070 at the former location of the MAWC well site in Springfield Township, Fayette County. A violation was issued in IR 4088070 for failure to restore the well site by 10/30/2025, in accordance with the 5/01/2025 amendment of the 12/16/2021 CO and A. The Department requested an NOV Response to IR 4088070 from the operator by December 4, 2025.The First Modification to the COA was entered on 5/01/2025. Paragraph 3i of the 12/16/2021 CO and A states: "M4 shall immediately commence work to completely restore the Well sites upon execution of the First Amendment and complete restoration of the Well Sites by October 30, 2025, in accordance with Section 3216 of the 2012 Oil and Gas act, 58 Pa.C.S. 3216, the site restoration regulations set forth in 25 Pa. Code 78a.65, and all applicable provisions of the Clean Streams Law and the regulations promulgated thereunder. M4 shall submit form 8000 PM-OOGN0075, "Well Site Restoration Report," within sixty (60) days of restoring the Well Sites." Site restoration is to be conducted "as closely to original conditions as practicable, including restoration of original contours and capability of supporting land uses existing prior to drilling of the Well(s) by October 30, 2025, unless M4 obtains a signed and notarized written consent of the landowner to leave the Well Site in an altered state".The following was observed:The Act 9 sign remains installed at the entrance of the access road (photo 1). No restoration plans were found on site during this inspection. Although site stabilization and progress of restoration could not be completely evaluated during this inspection due to the snow cover, it is still evident through the snow cover that the site has not attained greater than 70% uniform and adequate vegetative growth (photos 5, 8, and 9). The Department recommends that the operator assess the site for temporary stabilization upon dissipation of the snow cover, and apply additional mulch and seed if needed.Based on observations from this inspection, the violation issued in IR 4088070 shall remain outstanding.

properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: SCORPIO ENERGY INC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 11/21/2023
Violation Code: 102.4(b)1 - EROSION AND SEDIMENT CONTROL REQUIREMENTS - Person conducting earth disturbance activity failed to implement and maintain E & S BMPs to minimize the potential for accelerated erosion and sedimentation.
Violation ID: 8166116
Permit API: 053-31042
Unconventional: No
County: Forest
Municipality: Howe Township
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 11/21/2023
Comments: This site is in the process of being constructed for a conventional well. The template for the well site has been completed. The well site location and access road have not been stoned. There has been no drilling activity on site and the pit has not been dug. There was no activity on site during the time of the inspection. The drilling permit and Erosion and Sedimentation (E and S) Plan were posted at the entrance of the location.The road leading to the well site location did not have culverts, sumps, or ditches installed as outlined in the E and S Plan. There were no temporary BMPs in place at the time of the inspection. Areas of earth disturbance associated with the construction of the well site location were not seeded and mulched.At the time of inspection, the site showed evidence of accelerated erosion. Sediment laden water was flowing parallel to the access road along the bottom slope of the constructed bank (pictured in Photo 1). The sediment laden water was ponding at the lowest point on the well site location (pictured in Photo 2). Stormwater and sediment from the well sites under construction up slope of Hastings SDT 47 OG Well were also contributing to the accelerated erosion at the site (pictured in Photo 3). Due to the volume of water, overflow from the low point was discharging off the site location (pictured in Photo 4). The sediment laden water was flowing through the woods directly discharging into Hastings Run (pictured in Photo 5). The operator, Steven Tachoir, was contacted over a voicemail to discuss the results of this inspection. He has been advised to install temporary BMPs to prevent accelerated erosion until the permanent BMPs can be installed in accordance with the E and S Plan. He has also been advised to seed and mulch the areas of earth disturbance associated with construction of the well. It has been proposed to the operator to meet on site to further discuss options for remediation. Follow up inspections will continue to occur until the work has been completed.

Violation ID: 845829
Permit API: 047-23756
Unconventional: No
County: Elk
Municipality: Saint Marys City
Inspection Type: Complaint Inspection
Inspection Date: 2019-04-02
Comments: This inspection was performed following a report to the NWRO by Diversified Oil and Gas of a 25 gallon brine spill at their #38067 well. It appears as though a small leak formed in a 50 barrel poly tank over the winter, which allowed some production fluid to leach out slowly over time. Once the snow melted, the well tender noticed a small area (~10x10 ft) that had vegetation missing and deer prints. The diking was unlined, so it seems that production water had leached out, and high conductivity levels were noted in this area. All the brine stayed in a small area, and no waters are nearby to be a concern for migration. The operator has shut in this well for the time being, and excavation is scheduled for the week of 4/8. Continued inspection of this site will be performed at that time.

Comments: Onsite for an incident response to a reported release from the operator. The release was reported on 5/15/2020 at 13:45pm. The delay of site investigation/response was due to restrictions based upon the COVID 19 pandemic. The release occurred as a result of a 210bbl steel tank failure and it appears that the bottom of the tank had developed a hole and or multiple holes. It was reported that 30bbls was lost from the tank directly to the earthen dike substrate. The earthen dike area is designed in a manner with two levels, the oil tanks are located at a higher elevation than the brine storage tanks. Crude oil was observed seeping out of the rock substrate inside the dike down-gradient from the oil tanks. A small sump was dug to collect the oil and pumped into a poly tank. At the time of the inspection there is no visual indication that the oil has migrated outside of the earthen dike footprint/substrate. The department has requested that the operator remove the 210bbl steel tank and remove the impacted material. As well as recover as much oil as possible. At this time a formal written plan will not be required unless site conditions change or cleanup actions are not conducted in a timely manner. Violations are noted

Comments: On October 1, 2024, the Department conducted a routine inspection at the R Carlisle well pad in Hopewell Township, Washington County. Notice of Termination was approved for this site on October 28, 2016.The following was observed:The Act 9 sign is installed at the entrance of the access road and is not obscured from view by vegetation, in accordance with 78a.55 (see photo 1). Several portions of the access road are exhibiting severe accelerated erosion and sedimentation at the time of inspection (see photo 2). The well pad appears to be stable at the time of inspection with no accelerated erosion or sedimentation observed (see photo 3). Production tanks and the surrounding secondary containment do not have any observable fluid leaks (see photo 4). The GPU units onsite are not equipped with secondary containment (see photo 5). However, the wells onsite were drilled prior to the promulgation of 78a. No evidence of fluid leaks or discharge was observed on the ground around the GPU units. Well 7H is equipped with a well tag with no observable fluids leaking to the ground around it (see photos 7 and 8). There are four other well heads onsite that also appear to be equipped for production (see photo 6). Containment is staged adjacent to the production tanks, which appears to be for pumping operations. It is approximately half-full of rainwater at the time of inspection (see photo 9). The Emergency Response Plan (ERP) is onsite (see photo 10). Based on observations from this inspection, the Department recommends that secondary containments are kept empty so they are able to mitigate the risk of a release from occurring on site as intended. The Department also recommends that GPU units and other primary containments that store regulated substances are equipped with secondary containments to mitigate the risk of discharge to the ground and Waters of the Commonwealth.Violations are being issued against the severe accelerated erosion and sedimentation observed in the access road.

Comments: On January 3, 2023, the Department conducted an inspection on the Schimizzi S and M 1 well site in Hempfield Township, Westmoreland County. No evidence of leaks or discharge could be found around the new production tanks, and they appeared to be sound at the time of inspection. However, they were not equipped with secondary containment (see photos 3 and 8). Soil conductivity readings were taken in the earthen berms surrounding these tanks, and at the bases of these tanks (see photos 4-7). The well tag and required operator's information was present on the meter box (see photo 8). The Additional piping and production equipment was left onsite. Some tire rutting was observed at the back of the well site looking from the road, which could be due to third party traversing (see photo 10). The ground overall was soft, which could lead to future stabilization concerns. Therefore, the Department recommends that the operator take additional stabilization measures to prevent any potential E and S issues from developing.Based on observations from today's inspection, the violations that were continued in IR 3435475 shall remain outstanding, since no changes were made since and no NOV response has been received to date. An additional violation shall be issued against the production tanks, since they are not equipped with secondary containment in an unconventional site.

Comments: On 3/10/2023, DEP representative John Rogers conducted an Administrative inspection on the Chesapeake Floydie well site. This inspection is to report the results of two water samples that were collected from water puddles on the south corner and northeast side of the Floydie well site. During an inspection on 1/24/2023, the department discovered high conductance fluid on two areas of the well pad surface outside of containment. In the first area, the fluid covered a 6' x 10' area and field tested at 11.93 mS conductance with an Oakton PCTS-50 meter. The department collected water sample #9551-039 for laboratory analysis from location N 41.665131 W -76.126503. In the second area, the fluid covered a 10' x 10' area and field tested at 4.90 mS conductance with an Oakton PCTS-50 meter. This water puddle was in a larger muddy 35' x 20' area that field tested at over 4.0 mS conductance with a Hanna Groline meter. The department collected water sample #9551-040 from location N 41.66589 W -76.12645.On 2/25/2023 the department received the results of the laboratory analysis that shows elevated barium, strontium and lithium and is indicative of brine/production fluid being released onto the pad. The sample reports are displayed in pictures 1, 2, 3 and 4.Chesapeake is pursuing Act 2 for the site in response to that incident.The release of fluid with elevated conductance to the pad surface constitutes violations of SWMA 301, CSL 402, 25 PA Code 78a.56(a) and 78.66(b)(2).Violations are still outstanding for inspection ID 3492400 for elevated conductance fluid being discovered on the unprotected pad surface.

Comments: On 01/06/2026, an incident inspection was conducted at the Rough Hollow Well Site following receipt of a spill reported to the Department on 01/05/2026 (CTS 394427). I was accompanied by Ralph Barb and Laura Grada (PA DEP).The operator reported that approximately 5-10 gallons of production fluid was released to the pad. No waterways were affected and SPSI (cleanup crew) was on site.The Department contacted the operator on 01/06/2026 prior to inspection and received the following information:The release occurred within the GPU. The dump line failed within the unit.The release occurred within the gas production unit (GPU) associated with the Rough Hollow 593213- 12HU well (API - 059-27108). This wells GPU is not listed within the secondary containment Consent Order and Agreement (COA).The well was SPUD on 09/30/2016.The operator determined the amount released visually; however, they are working to determine the exact amount that was released.Excavation is on hold until the operator can determine the exact quantity released and if additional excavation is necessary.The following was observed during inspection on 01/06/2026:The Act 9 sign was at the site entrance. The Emergency Response Plan was on site (Photos 1, 2).The spill was observed adjacent to GPU 12H. The impacted area was excavated and sumps dug. Permit API: 015-23430
Unconventional: Yes

Inspection Type: Administrative/File Review
Inspection Date: 2020-04-27
Comments: In an effort to prevent the spread of the COVID-19 virus, the Department has conducted this administrative inspection in response to information provided by Chief. Based on the analytical results for isotopic samples collected by Chief at the above-referenced well on 6/17/2019 and 11/15/2019, methane was detected as follows: 25.13 % Methane detected at the Intermediate (9 5/8¿) x Surface (13 3/8¿) casing annulus on 6/17/2019. 0.37 % Methane detected at the Surface casing (13 3/8¿) x Conductor (20¿) annulus on 11/15/2019. 98.26 % Methane detected at the Production (5 ½") x Intermediate (9 5/8¿) casing annulus on 11/15/2019. The presence of methane at the Surface casing (13 3/8¿) x Conductor (20¿) is evidence of defective cement with methane outside of the surface casing string. As a result, violations of 25 Pa. Code §78a.73(b), §78a81(a)(2) and (3), and §78a.85(a)(5) have been cited. Please note that because your company provided a self-reported notification, no violation was cited for 25 Pa. Code §78a.86, defective cement, for the other annuli where methane was detected. However, Chief is required to comply with the Department¿s regulations, 25 Pa. Code §78a.86, which provides: ¿In a well that has defective, insufficient or improperly cemented casing, the operator shall report the defect to the Department within 24 hours of discovery by the operator and shall correct the defect. The operator shall correct the defect or submit a plan to correct the defect for approval by the Department within 30 days. If the defect cannot be corrected or an alternate method is not approved by the Department, the well shall be plugged under § 78a.91 ¿ 78a.98 (related to plugging).¿ Therefore, please provide a written response within 30 days of receipt of this Notice of Violation, as to when and how the above listed violations were or will be corrected, and what steps are being taken to prevent their recurrence.

Comments: On April 20, 2022, Beech Resources Don Stevenson notified DEP through the spill notification line (CTS #363517) that about 15 gallons of synthetic based mud was spilled outside of containment onto the well pad surface at the ISA Well Pad. The spill occurred when a hose ruptured during a transfer of the base mud to a tanker truck which was outside containment on the well pad. The area of impact appeared to be 15 ft. by 15 ft. from the evidence in the pictures provided by Don Stevenson of Beech Resources. The base mud was immediately contained and removed from the pad surface. The impacted soil from the spill was immediately removed from the pad surface by Beech Resources. Violations of Clean Streams Law 402(b), Chapter 78a.56(a), and Soild Waste Management Act Section 301 have been immediately corrected.
